column1: # How a number a caller writes into an open payload is read, before anything is sealed (issue #75).
# `google.protobuf.Struct` carries every number as a double, so `{"score": 1.0}` and
# `{"score": 1}` are the same eight bytes on the wire and cannot be told apart again.
# Rather than let the distinction be decided by which engine answered, it is decided at
# ingress, the same way everywhere: a whole-valued number is read whole, and a number a
# double can no longer count one at a time is refused rather than quietly rounded.
# Two implementations follow this file, and a test in each pins it against these rows:
#   crates/made-mcp/src/protocol/struct_numbers.rs      — both MCP arms, at the request gate
#   crates/made-adapters/src/grpc/mappers/attributes.rs — the gRPC server, for direct clients
# Every row is a number both implementations can be handed as written. An integer past
# 2^53 is not one of those — it reaches the gRPC server already rounded, because the wire
# rounded it, which is the whole reason the range is refused rather than trusted. That
# case is pinned where it can be: in `struct_numbers.rs`, against what a client sends.
# read_as: the JSON the value is read as; empty for a refusal.
